chunks: By Allah, if your hearts were to melt thoroughly, and your eyes shed tears of blood from hope for Him and fear of Him, and then you were granted long life in this world as long as it lasts, your actions would not repay the great bounties He has bestowed upon you, and His guiding you to faith, even if you did not leave any of your effort.
ai.seo_question: How can human actions repay the immense bounties of God according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs hyperbolic imagery of hearts crumbling and eyes weeping blood to illustrate that even a lifetime of exhaustive worship cannot repay the primordial favor of divine guidance (hudan) to faith. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on God's grace (fadl) preceding human effort, suggesting that true gratitude is not merely transactional repayment but a recognition of the foundational gift of iman itself.
